category: Embed protocol messages and HTML viewer options
description: Field-level reference for the JSON postMessage protocol used by embed.diagrams.net (host actions, editor events, export formats and layout presets) and for the read-only HTML viewer (viewer.min.js / GraphViewer) whose behaviour is configured through the data-mxgraph JSON attribute. Use it when writing an integration that hosts the editor or renders diagrams inside a web page.

tools.name: embed action: load (content fields)
tools.description: The first message the host sends after the init event. It carries the diagram either as xml (an <mxfile> or <mxGraphModel> string, may be compressed) or as descriptor {format, data, wrap} for other formats, plus document-level options: autosave (1 enables autosave events), modified (custom resource key), saveAndExit, noSaveBtn, noExitBtn, title (shown in the toolbar) and libs (semicolon list of libraries to show). An empty xml loads a blank diagram.

parameters.name: xml
parameters.description: Diagram XML; empty string for a new diagram.

parameters.name: descriptor
parameters.description: {format, data, wrap} alternative to xml (e.g. format 'png' with embedded diagram).

parameters.name: autosave
parameters.description: 1 makes the editor emit autosave events after each change.

parameters.name: modified
parameters.description: Resource key of the unsaved-changes message, or 0.

parameters.name: saveAndExit / noSaveBtn / noExitBtn
parameters.description: Per-document toolbar flags (same as the URL parameters).

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Document title shown in the editor.

parameters.name: libs
parameters.description: Semicolon-separated library keys to show in the sidebar.

tools.notes: The editor answers with a load event carrying bounds, scale and page information. Send load again to replace the content; use merge to update in place.

tools.name: embed action: load (appearance and viewport fields)
tools.description: Additional load fields that control how the loaded diagram is presented: dark (0/1/auto), theme, rough and toSketch (convert to sketch style), border, background (page colour), viewport {x,y,width,height}, rect, minWidth/minHeight, viewbox, scale, scaleBorder, fit and maxFitScale (fit the diagram on load), scroll, publishClose, sourceMetadata, exportProtocol, diffSync (enable checksum-based patch synchronisation) and layout (layouts to apply once loaded).
tools.usage: {action: 'load', xml: '...', dark: 'auto', fit: true, maxFitScale: 2, border: 20, diffSync: true, layout: [{layout: 'mxHierarchicalLayout', config: {orientation: 'north'}}]}

parameters.name: fit / maxFitScale / scale / viewbox / viewport / rect
border / background
parameters.description: Canvas margin and page background colour.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.description: Array of {layout, config} applied after loading, or a preset name.

tools.notes: Fields are optional; unknown fields are ignored. toSketch rewrites cell styles, so use it only for whiteboard-style hosts.

tools.name: embed export formats (xml, json, svg, xmlsvg, png, xmlpng, html, html2)
tools.description: Values of the format field in the host's export action and the editor's export event: xml (diagram XML), json (JSON with xml plus page/bounds data), svg (plain SVG), xmlsvg (SVG with the diagram embedded in its content attribute, i.e. a .drawio.svg), png (PNG data URI), xmlpng (PNG with embedded diagram, .drawio.png), html and html2 (self-contained HTML viewer page). The export event returns the result in data (data URI or text) together with xml.

parameters.name: svg / xmlsvg
parameters.description: Vector output; xmlsvg keeps the editable source.

parameters.name: png / xmlpng
parameters.description: Raster data URI; xmlpng keeps the editable source in a PNG chunk.

parameters.name: html / html2
parameters.description: Standalone HTML page with the viewer.

tools.example:
postMessage(JSON.stringify({action: 'export', format: 'xmlpng', spin: 'Updating preview', scale: 2}), '*');
// editor replies: {event: 'export', format: 'xmlpng', data: 'data:image/png;base64,...', xml: '<mxfile>...'}
tools.notes: Hosts typically request xmlpng or xmlsvg after each save so the stored image doubles as the editable source. PDF is not available through the embed protocol.

tools.name: embed export options (scale, border, layerIds, pageId, allPages, embedImages, keepTheme, transparent, background, selection)
tools.description: Optional fields of the export action: spin/spinKey and message/messageKey (spinner text), scale, width, border, shadow, grid, keepTheme (keep dark-mode colours), transparent, background, size, layerIds (array of layer ids to render), pageId or currentPage (which page), allPages, withSvg, embedImages, embedFonts, embedCellMetadata, includeData, compressed (compress the returned xml), selection (export only selected cells) and xml (export a given XML instead of the current diagram).
tools.usage: {action: 'export', format: 'png', scale: 2, border: 10, transparent: true, layerIds: ['1'], pageId: 'p2', embedImages: true, keepTheme: false}

parameters.name: layerIds / pageId / currentPage / allPages
parameters.description: What part of the document to render.

parameters.name: selection
parameters.description: true exports only the current selection.

parameters.name: compressed
parameters.description: true returns compressed XML in the xml field.

tools.notes: Fonts are embedded as data URIs when embedFonts is true, which increases size but makes the SVG portable.

tools.name: embed action: fit
tools.description: Zooms and scrolls the editor so the whole diagram is visible, with optional border (px) and maxScale (upper zoom bound so small diagrams are not blown up). The editor confirms with a fit event that includes the new bounds, scale and translate.

parameters.name: border
parameters.description: Margin in px around the fitted diagram.

tools.notes: Send after the container has been resized; the load action's fit field does the same once at load time.

tools.name: embed actions: viewbox and viewport
tools.description: viewbox scrolls/zooms to a rectangle {x, y, width, height, border} in diagram coordinates and replies with a viewbox event; viewport tells the editor the visible region of its container {x, y, width, height} in pixels (used by inline embeds where the iframe is larger than the visible area) so fit and dialogs are positioned correctly.
tools.usage:
{action: 'viewbox', viewbox: {x: 0, y: 0, width: 800, height: 600, border: 20}}
{action: 'viewport', viewport: {x: 0, y: 0, width: 1200, height: 700}}

parameters.name: viewbox
parameters.description: Region to show (diagram units) plus optional border.

tools.notes: Equivalent to the ?viewbox= URL parameter and the viewbox custom-link action.

tools.name: embed action: resetEditor
tools.description: Clears the current document, undo history and modified state so the same iframe can be reused for another diagram without reloading the page. Follow it with a new load action.
tools.notes: Faster than recreating the iframe, which reloads several megabytes of JavaScript.

tools.name: embed action: invokeAction
tools.description: Runs one of the editor's named actions (the same ids used by menus and keyboard shortcuts, e.g. selectAll, undo, redo, zoomIn, fitWindow, toFront, layers, formatPanel, print, exportSvg) from the host page, so a host toolbar can drive the editor without emulating clicks.
tools.notes: Action ids can be discovered from the keyboard-shortcut labels or by listing ui.actions.actions in a plugin.

tools.name: embed action: textContent (and textContent event)
tools.description: Asks the editor for the plain text of all labels in the diagram; the editor replies with {event: 'textContent', data: '<text>'}. Hosts use it for search indexing, accessibility descriptions or AI summaries without parsing the XML themselves.
tools.notes: Only the current page is included. The 'text' plugin offers the same extraction interactively (Extras > Extract Text).

tools.name: embed action: snapshot
tools.description: Requests a lightweight snapshot of the current state; the editor responds through the export/save pipeline with the current XML so a host can persist a checkpoint (for example before closing) without waiting for the next autosave.
tools.notes: For deterministic saving prefer autosave:1 in load and handle the autosave/save events.

tools.name: embed action: fullscreenChanged (and resize event)
tools.description: The editor emits {event: 'resize', fullscreen, rect} when its inline window is resized or toggled to fullscreen; the host answers or initiates with {action: 'fullscreenChanged', value: true|false} so both sides agree on the layout. Used by inline embeds (embedInline=1) that let users expand the editor.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: true when the host has put the editor into fullscreen.

tools.notes: Only relevant for inline/embedded windows, not for full-page iframes.

tools.name: embed actions: remoteInvoke and remoteInvokeReady
tools.description: Reverse RPC channel: after the host sends remoteInvokeReady, the editor may call host functions with {action: 'remoteInvoke', functionName, functionArgs} and the host replies {action: 'remoteInvokeResponse', resp, error}. draw.io's own Confluence/Jira apps use it for file pickers and attachment access; custom hosts can expose any function set.

parameters.name: functionName
parameters.description: Name of the host function requested by the editor.

parameters.name: resp / error
parameters.description: Result or error returned by the host.

tools.notes: Messages carry msgMarkers that must be echoed so the editor can match responses to calls.

tools.name: embed event: openLink
tools.description: Sent when the user clicks a link inside the diagram and the editor is not allowed to open windows itself (URL parameter suppressNewWindows=1 or the configuration key). The message contains href, target and allowOpener so the host can open the link in its own way (routing, permission checks, same-tab navigation).

parameters.name: allowOpener
parameters.description: Whether the new window may keep window.opener.

tools.notes: Page links (data:page/id,...) are handled inside the editor and do not trigger this event.

tools.name: embed event: load (bounds, modelBounds, scale, translate, page fields)
tools.description: Reply to a successful load action (and the common tail of autosave, save, export, layout, fit and viewbox events): bounds (rendered bounds in px), modelBounds (diagram units), scale, translate, pageVisible, currentPage (index), page (id), containerSize and, when diffSync is on, checksum. Hosts use bounds/containerSize to size previews and to decide whether to call fit.
tools.usage: {event: 'load', bounds: {x,y,width,height}, modelBounds: {x,y,width,height}, scale: 1, translate: {x,y}, pageVisible: true, currentPage: 0, page: 'p1', containerSize: {width,height}, checksum: '...'}

parameters.name: bounds / modelBounds
parameters.description: Diagram extent in screen px and in model units.

parameters.name: currentPage / page / pageVisible
parameters.description: Page index, page id and page-view flag.

tools.notes: returnbounds=1 in the URL adds the same fields to messages that would otherwise omit them.

tools.name: embed events: patch, getDiff, resetDiff (diffSync)
tools.description: With diffSync enabled in load, the host can push incremental changes instead of whole files: action patch {patch, checksum} applies a diff and the editor answers {event: 'patch', checksum, message, checksumMismatch}; action getDiff returns {event: 'getDiff', patch, checksum} (or xml when no diff is possible); action resetDiff {xml} resets the baseline and answers {event: 'resetDiff', checksum}. Autosave events then include patch and checksum fields too.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: Diff object in draw.io's own patch format (as produced by getDiff/autosave).

parameters.name: checksum
parameters.description: Checksum of the state the patch applies to; mismatch is reported.

tools.notes: Intended for real-time collaboration back ends; simpler hosts can ignore diffSync and use full XML.

tools.name: embed layout presets (verticalFlow, horizontalFlow, verticalTree, horizontalTree, radialTree, organic)
tools.description: Names accepted by the layout action ({action: 'layout', layouts: [...]}) and by the layout field of load and create=. A preset string runs the corresponding Arrange > Layout algorithm on the whole diagram; a {layout, config} object names an mxGraph layout class (mxHierarchicalLayout, mxCompactTreeLayout, mxRadialTreeLayout, mxFastOrganicLayout, mxCircleLayout) with constructor properties in config. The editor answers with a layout event.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Properties applied to the layout instance (e.g. orientation, levelDistance, nodeDistance, forceConstant, radius).

tools.example: postMessage(JSON.stringify({action: 'layout', layouts: [{layout: 'mxCompactTreeLayout', config: {horizontal: false, levelDistance: 60, nodeDistance: 30}}]}), '*');
tools.notes: Layouts are applied to the current page and recorded in the undo history.

tools.name: embed event: template (fields)
tools.description: Result of the template action (which opens the Templates dialog inside the editor). For built-in or blank choices the event carries xml, blank, name, tempUrl, libs and builtIn; when the user picks a host-provided template it carries docUrl, info and name. The host loads the returned xml or fetches docUrl and then sends load.
tools.usage: {action: 'template', callback: true, templatesOnly: true, enableRecent: true, enableSearch: true, enableCustomTemp: true}   ->   {event: 'template', xml, blank, name, tempUrl, libs, builtIn}

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: true returns the choice to the host instead of loading it directly.

parameters.name: templatesOnly / enableRecent / enableSearch / enableCustomTemp / withoutType / noExitOnCancel
xml / blank / name / tempUrl / libs / builtIn

tools.example: if (msg.event === 'template') { postMessage(JSON.stringify({action: 'load', xml: msg.xml || '', title: msg.name}), '*'); }
tools.notes: Custom template sets come from the configuration keys templateFile and customTemplates.

tools.name: embed events: prompt, prompt-cancel and draft results
tools.description: Responses to host dialogs: the prompt action ({title, ok, defaultValue}) yields {event: 'prompt', value, message} when confirmed or {event: 'prompt-cancel', message} when dismissed; the draft action (offering to restore an unsaved draft: {xml, name, editKey, discardKey, ignore}) yields {event: 'draft', result: 'Edit'|'Discard'|'ignore', message}. The message field echoes the original request so hosts can correlate.
tools.usage:
{action: 'prompt', title: 'File name', ok: 'Save', defaultValue: 'diagram.drawio'}   ->   {event: 'prompt', value: 'diagram.drawio'}
{action: 'draft', xml: draftXml, name: 'diagram.drawio'}   ->   {event: 'draft', result: 'Edit'}

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Edit, Discard or ignore for draft dialogs.

tools.example: if (msg.event === 'draft') { if (msg.result === 'Edit') load(draftXml); else if (msg.result === 'Discard') load(savedXml); }
tools.notes: dialog and status actions have no reply.

tools.name: viewer.min.js script and the .mxgraph div
tools.description: The read-only HTML viewer is a single script (https://viewer.diagrams.net/js/viewer-static.min.js, or viewer.min.js from a self-hosted instance) that, on load, turns every <div class="mxgraph"> whose data-mxgraph attribute holds a JSON configuration into an interactive diagram. File > Embed > HTML generates this markup with the diagram XML inlined; the same script can be loaded once for many diagrams on a page.

parameters.name: class="mxgraph"
parameters.description: Marker class the script looks for (GraphViewer.processElements).

parameters.name: data-mxgraph
parameters.description: HTML-escaped JSON configuration (keys documented in the data-mxgraph entries).

tools.notes: viewer-static.min.js is self-contained (fonts and images embedded); viewer.min.js loads resources relative to its host. The Docker image serves both under /js/.

tools.name: GraphViewer.createViewerForElement
tools.description: Programmatic entry point of the viewer script: creates a viewer for one DOM element that carries a data-mxgraph attribute (or after you set it) and invokes an optional callback with the GraphViewer instance, whose graph property is the underlying mxGraph. Use it for diagrams inserted dynamically after page load, e.g. in single-page applications.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: DOM element with a data-mxgraph JSON attribute.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: Optional function receiving the created GraphViewer.

tools.notes: The script auto-processes elements present at load time; call this only for elements added later.

tools.name: GraphViewer.processElements
tools.description: Scans the document for elements with the given class name (default mxgraph) and creates a viewer for each one that has not been processed yet. The viewer script calls it once on load; call it again after injecting several diagrams at once, or with a custom class name to use different markup.

parameters.name: classname
parameters.description: CSS class to look for; defaults to 'mxgraph'.

tools.notes: Elements already converted are skipped, so repeated calls are safe.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: xml / url
tools.description: Source of the diagram for the HTML viewer: xml holds the diagram XML inline (HTML-escaped inside the attribute; compressed <mxfile> content is accepted) and url points to a .drawio/.xml/.svg/.png file that the viewer fetches; url takes precedence over xml. Remote files must be served with CORS headers.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute URL of the diagram file (CORS required).

tools.notes: Using url keeps the HTML small and lets the diagram update without regenerating the page.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: highlight
tools.description: Colour (with leading #) used to outline cells that carry links when hovered in the HTML viewer, matching the highlight= URL parameter of the lightbox. Set it to a colour that contrasts with the diagram's palette so clickable shapes are discoverable.
tools.notes: show-link-icons: true is the always-visible alternative.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: nav / move
tools.description: nav: true enables collapse/expand of containers and tree folding in the HTML viewer (nav: false disables it, the default); move: true additionally lets a collapse/expand shift sibling cells to close gaps, as in the editor's tree folding.
tools.notes: Same as the nav=1 URL parameter for lightbox links.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: resize / auto-fit / allow-zoom-in / allow-zoom-out
tools.description: Sizing behaviour: resize: true lets the container grow to the diagram size, resize: false keeps the container as laid out; auto-fit: true (default) scales the diagram to fit the container width; allow-zoom-in: true forces auto-fit and permits scale factors above 1 for small diagrams; allow-zoom-out controls whether large diagrams may be shrunk. Together they decide whether a page reflows around the diagram or the diagram adapts to the page.
tools.notes: responsive: true with responsive-max-scale is a newer alternative that re-fits on window resize.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: toolbar
tools.description: Space-separated list of toolbar tools shown above (or inline with) the diagram: pages (page selector), zoom (zoom in/out/reset), layers (layer visibility), tags, lightbox (open in the fullscreen lightbox) and custom (buttons from toolbar-buttons). Omit the key for no toolbar; toolbar-nohide and toolbar-position tune its display.

parameters.name: layers / tags
parameters.description: Visibility controls for layers and tags.

parameters.name: lightbox
parameters.description: Button to open the lightbox viewer.

tools.notes: The lightbox button opens viewer.diagrams.net (or the URL configured by DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL on self-hosted instances).

tools.name: data-mxgraph: toolbar-buttons
tools.description: Defines custom toolbar buttons used when toolbar contains 'custom': an object keyed by button id whose values give title, image (data URI or URL of the icon), handler (JavaScript function or function name) and optional enabled flag. Lets a host page add 'Edit', 'Download' or application-specific buttons next to the built-in tools.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Function called with the GraphViewer when clicked.

tools.notes: Handlers named as strings are resolved on window; functions must be attached before the viewer script runs.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: toolbar-nohide / toolbar-position
tools.description: toolbar-nohide: true keeps the toolbar permanently visible instead of showing it only on hover; toolbar-position selects top (default, above the diagram), inline (overlaid on the diagram) or bottom. Use nohide for touch devices where hover is unavailable.
tools.notes: Ignored when no toolbar is configured.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: edit / editable
tools.description: edit gives the URL for an 'Edit' button in the lightbox opened from the viewer (edit: "_blank" opens a copy in a new editor tab); editable: false removes that button so viewers cannot open the diagram in an editor. Hosts with their own edit flow set edit to their route.

parameters.name: editable
parameters.description: false disables editing from the lightbox (default true).

tools.notes: Mirrors the edit= URL parameter.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: lightbox
tools.description: Controls what a click on the diagram or the lightbox toolbar button does: by default the lightbox opens as an overlay in the same page; lightbox: false disables it (the diagram is static) and lightbox: "open" forces it to open in a new window, which avoids overlay/CSP problems in restrictive host pages.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: Open the lightbox in a new window.

tools.notes: The lightbox URL is viewer.diagrams.net unless the script was built with a different base (DRAWIO_LIGHTBOX_URL).

tools.name: data-mxgraph: zoom / border / center / max-height
tools.description: Initial presentation: zoom (initial scale, default 1, ignored when auto-fit applies), border (padding in px around the diagram, default 8), center: true (centre the diagram horizontally in a wider container; forceCenter and hCenterOnly refine it) and max-height (maximum initial height in px, after which the viewer scrolls or scales).

parameters.name: max-height
parameters.description: Cap on the initial height in px.

tools.notes: max-height is the usual way to keep tall diagrams from dominating a documentation page.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: page / pageId / layers / layer-ids
tools.description: Selection of content: page (0-based index of the page to show, default 0) or pageId (the <diagram id>), layers (space-separated list of layer indexes to make visible initially) or layer-ids (space-separated layer cell ids). Combine with the layers toolbar tool to let readers toggle the rest.
tools.notes: Layer indexes follow the order of layer cells under root; ids are stable across reordering.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: title / tooltips / show-link-icons / show-tooltip-icons
tools.description: title sets the toolbar title (and tooltip via titleTooltip); tooltips: false suppresses cell tooltips; show-link-icons: true and show-tooltip-icons: true draw overlay icons on cells that have links or tooltips so readers can find them without hovering (show-note-icons does the same for notes).

parameters.name: show-link-icons / show-tooltip-icons / show-note-icons
parameters.description: Overlay icons for links, tooltips and notes.

tools.notes: Tooltips come from the tooltip attribute of an <object>-wrapped cell or from Edit > Edit Tooltip.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: target
tools.description: Where links inside the embedded diagram open: self (same window), blank (new window) or auto (default: external links in a new window, page links in place). Set self when the diagram serves as in-page navigation.
tools.notes: Same values as the target= URL parameter.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: auto-crop / check-visible-state
tools.description: auto-crop: true re-crops the visible area to the currently visible layers whenever layers are toggled, so hidden layers do not leave empty space; check-visible-state: false disables the delayed rendering that normally waits until the element scrolls into view (useful when the viewer is inside a hidden tab whose size is unknown).
tools.notes: Rendering inside display:none containers gives zero-size diagrams; disable check-visible-state and call GraphViewer.processElements after showing the container.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: dark-mode / responsive / responsive-max-scale
tools.description: dark-mode: true (or "auto") renders the diagram with dark-mode colours (cells using default colours adapt); responsive: true makes the viewer re-fit the diagram whenever the container size changes, with responsive-max-scale capping the zoom used when fitting. Both are read from the data-mxgraph JSON of current viewer builds.
tools.notes: Older viewer builds ignore these keys silently.

tools.name: data-mxgraph: hiddenTags
tools.description: Array of tag names whose cells start hidden in the HTML viewer, complementing the tags toolbar tool that lets readers toggle them. Tags are assigned in the editor with Edit > Edit Tags (Ctrl+K) and stored in the tags attribute of the cell.
tools.notes: The lightbox equivalent is the tags= URL parameter with a JSON value.
